The bright field (a) and dark field (b) HRTEM images of the AA6111 HS2-T6 alloy at the magnification of 310000×. 4.2 Apply the macro→micro scheme to calibrate the fracture criterion of the matrix materials 4.2.1 Tension test Before setting up for the macro model, it is important to obtain the material plastic flow behavior and it is usually performed through tensile tests. For this purpose, Ford has tensile-tested the AA6111 HS2-T6 alloy using … tensile test machine at a constant cross-head speed of … with ASTM E-8 standard tensile specimen as shown in Fig. 5, which has a gauge length of 57 mm and width of 12.5 mm. Flat ASTM E8 tensile coupons were electro discharged machined (EDM’d) from the supplied sheet materials. The coupons were cut in three different directions, where the tensile axis was either 0° (longitudinal, L), 45° (diagonal, D), or 90° (transverse, T) to the rolling direction. A portion of the tensile coupons were artificially aged at 180°C +/- 2°C for 8 hours to a T6 temper using a Blue M electric convection air furnace. Tensile specimens were tensile tested at a constant rate of 3.0 mm/min until failure using a servohydraulic MTS load frame. Surface strain of the gauge region was measured during the tensile tests using an ARAMIS 3D 5M stereo camera digital image correlation (DIC) system using GOM Correlate Pro 2021 software. Two Schneider Xenoplane 23 mm f1.4 camera lens were used, each mounted to an ARAMIS 5M (GigE), 5 Megapixel sensor. The two sensor-lens assemblies were mounted on an adjustable bar so that the camera distance—defined as—the minimum distance between the center of the sensor housings, was 165 mm. The working measurement distance—defined as—the distance from the midpoint of the camera distance to the middle of the tensile specimen, was 460 mm. The angle between the two optical camera axes was 25. 189°. Using this configuration, the system was calibrated using the cp20-175mmx140mm calibration panel, which resulted in a calibrated measurement volume of 145 mm long, 125 mm wide, and 105 mm deep.
